$comment: Canonical response security-header values for my-web-2026 (Issue #449). This file is the single source of truth: src/http/security-headers.ts emits these values for every Worker-generated response, and scripts/check-security-headers.mjs asserts that public/_headers carries the same strings for Cloudflare Static Assets. Editing a value here without editing public/_headers (or the reverse) fails `pnpm run validate:fast`.

referrer_policy.$comment: `host` is the fallback for every Worker-generated response. `tool_app` is used for a Tool artifact served under the manifest's delivery.artifact_path (/tools/<slug>/app/...); a Tool bundle is third-party-shaped content and must not leak the host URL to whatever it fetches.

$denied_permissions_rationale: The list is deliberately explicit and minimal rather than a blanket deny-all. A feature that is NOT listed keeps the browser default allowlist ('self'), so a future Tool that needs a new capability does not have to amend the host baseline first. Each listed feature has no plausible use on this site: bluetooth/hid/serial/usb are hardware bridges, camera/display-capture/geolocation/microphone are capture devices, payment and xr-spatial-tracking are platform-gated products. microphone is listed because at least one registered Tool (mic-level) needs it — that is exactly why the grant is per-Tool (delivery.iframe.allow in src/tools/manifest.json) rather than host-wide. Issue #817 (second wave) added NO feature to this list: the capability pi-game needs (fullscreen) cannot be granted by this header for a sandboxed frame, so it belongs to `sandbox_only_capabilities` instead.
$sandbox_only_capabilities_rationale: A capability whose grant is NOT a header. Three kinds live here, all measured on Chromium (Issue #817, second wave; Issue #772 adds `modals`): (1) `downloads` — the HTML sandbox token `allow-downloads` is what lets a framed document save a file, and Permissions-Policy has no `downloads` feature at all, so writing `downloads=()` into the header would make every browser log 'Unrecognized feature: downloads' on every response — site-wide console noise for a grant the header cannot express. (2) `fullscreen` — the container half (`<iframe allow="fullscreen">` + the `allowfullscreen` attribute) is what grants it, and the header CANNOT re-grant it to a sandboxed frame: the frame runs in an OPAQUE origin (sandbox without `allow-same-origin`), so an explicit `fullscreen=(self "https://rebuildup.dev")` does not match it — measured: the request fails with 'Disallowed by permissions policy'. The default allowlist ('self') does match the opaque frame, so the feature must NOT be denied anywhere: listing it in `denied_permissions` would kill it site-wide. (3) `modals` — `modals` is not a Permissions-Policy feature NAME at all, so the `allow` attribute is inert (measured: console warning 'Unrecognized feature: modals.'); what actually lets a framed Tool call `confirm()` / `alert()` is the HTML sandbox token `allow-modals`, and a sandboxed frame without it silently returns false from `confirm()` (measured A/B on history-quiz: docs/verification/tools/history-quiz-host-activation.md). All three are therefore declared in `delivery.iframe.allow` (the embed policy requires a capability name beside a conditional sandbox token, Issue #465) and granted by the sandbox token / the container attribute alone; `scripts/check-security-headers.mjs` expects NO Permissions-Policy on such a Tool's artefact, and refuses a deny baseline that lists them.
